summary: 4 findings, all fixed and each reproduced first as a failing test on the unchanged code. F1: main released a claim on the remembered answer of a busy bridge, so a peer was told it may take a file the session had started writing since. F2: a retire that found the file being written left the running call's taken-over claim in place, so the call failing gave the committed claim back. F3: main remembered committed claims without the omp load, so a restarted omp's restored claim (stamps from 1 again) was retired for an earlier load's commit while git failed, and the session's uncommitted write lost its claim. With the fixes the five frozen properties hold for one file, two agents, one restart, 2 calls and 2 world events (2.0M states, depth 46) and for 3 calls, own commits, one restart and 3 world events (157M states, depth 60); 11 of 11 mutations are detected (each 27 Oct regression and F1 to F4 among them), 1 declared equivalent. F4 (found in review of the first model, which left the session's own git runs out): a commit of the session's own that succeeded dropped a file a call begun before it was still writing, so that call's landed write was nobody's claim; the model now has the session's own commit calls (3 calls, 23.3M states, depth 53).

findings.title: A busy bridge's remembered answer released a file the session had started writing
findings.story: Main reads A's claims (F, edited earlier). While main waits for git, A starts `sleep 8; echo x > f`: its hook claims F with a new stamp. Main tells B that F is A's. The person commits the earlier edit. On the next pass A's bridge is busy and main judges its remembered answer, which shows F not pending; git lists F clean, so main tells B that F is nobody's while A's command is still about to write it, and B's guard lets B drop or overwrite F.

fix.summary: judgeClaim releases a claim only on the bridge's own answer of this pass (`fresh`); a remembered answer only keeps claims.

findings.title: A failed call gave back a claim main had judged committed
findings.story: A edited F; the person committed it. While main waits for git, A starts an edit of F that will fail: the hook claims F with a new stamp and remembers the committed claim as the one it took over. Main retires the committed stamp; the ledger keeps F (a call writes it). The edit fails and reverts F to the claim it took over, the committed one. When B then changes F, A's book holds a claim on B's change; only main's memory of the commit hides it, and a restart of main loses that.

reproduction.test: src/main/checkout-peers.test.ts 'never gives back a committed claim when the call that took it over fails'

fix.summary: ClaimBook.retire voids the taken-over claim of a running call when that claim is the one retired.

findings.title: A restarted omp's restored claim was retired for an earlier load's commit
findings.story: A restored claim (stamp 1) is committed and main remembers member, file and stamp 1 as committed. A changes F again and the omp restarts: the journal restores F as stamp 1 under a new instance. Git times out; main finds member, file and stamp 1 in its memory, judges the claim committed and retires it with the new instance, which the bridge accepts. A's uncommitted change is no longer A's, and B may overwrite it.

reproduction.test: src/main/checkout-peers.test.ts 'never retires a restarted omp's claim on what git said of the claim its earlier load had'

fix.summary: #committed keys carry the instance; a claim judged committed stays committed while its load and stamp stand.

findings.title: The session's own commit dropped a file a call begun before it was still writing
findings.story: A starts `sleep 8; echo x > f` (W): its hook claims f. A commit of f in another call of A's succeeds before W's bytes land; #clean drops f because f's stamp is not newer than the commit's start, although W still writes it. W's bytes land and W reports back; its confirm moves only stamps that exist, so f, now uncommitted again, is nobody's claim and a peer may overwrite it.

reproduction.test: src/main/bridge-checkout-peers-claims.test.ts 'keeps a file a call started earlier is still writing' and 'goes back to no claim when an edit that began before the session's commit writes nothing'

fix.summary: #clean leaves a file a running call writes and voids the claim that call took over.
